newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates jump in week.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates jump in week.

text.p: Average commitment rates on U.S. 30-year fixed rate mortgages jumped to an average 7.84 percent from 7.65 percent the previous week, while 15-year rates climbed to 7.35 percent from 7.15 percent, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
One-year adjustable-rate mortgages also rose to 5.54 percent from 5.49 percent last week, it said.
A year ago, the 30-year loan rate averaged 7.38 percent, the 15-year 6.87 percent and the ARM 5.40 percent.

"As expected, interest rates rose considerably after (Federal Reserve) Chairman Alan Greenspan warned the financial markets to exercise caution last week," Frank Nothaft, Freddie Mac deputy chief economist, said.
Nothaft added that it is very likely "rates will continue to rise over the next few weeks."
Greenspan on Wednesday gave the second leg of seminannual Humphrey Hawkins economic testimony to Congress, leaving many economists and traders anticipating a Fed rate hike soon.
On Friday the Labor Department will issue unemployment data for February.
Lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.4 percent on the ARM, also unchanged from the prior week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
